title: Corporate Takeover Bids, Methods of Payment, and Bidding Firms' Stock Returns

rival_explanations: higher probability of failure of stock exchange offers relative to cash offers driving their negative returns
type of acquisition (tender offer versus merger) rather than method of payment driving the abnormal returns

context.industry_setting: cross-industry (NYSE/AMEX-listed bidding firms; no focal sector)
context.sample_description: Bidding firms engaged in successful takeovers (tender offers or mergers), identified from the July 1981 FTC Statistical Report on Mergers and Acquisitions and the Wall Street Journal Index, with daily stock returns available on the CRSP tapes; screened to exclude firms with concurrent major corporate events
context.sample_size: 167 acquiring firms (60 stock exchange offers, 100 cash offers, 7 combinations)

data_sources.name: Center for Research in Security Prices (CRSP)
W. T. Grimm & Co. Mergerstat Review

analyses.label: Table III - Event Study Analysis: Overall Results (60 stock exchange offers vs 100 cash offers)

dv.name: bidding firms' common stock abnormal returns

key_ivs.name: method of payment (stock exchange offer vs cash offer)
key_ivs.source: Wall Street Journal Index and SEC forms 13D and 14D

analyses.label: [withheld: wording matches the source]
analyses.sample: successful takeovers classified by type of acquisition x method of payment: merger stock exchange (60), merger cash (64), tender combinations (5), tender cash (36)

dv.name: bidding firms' common stock abnormal returns
dv.measure: daily average abnormal return (AR) computed from the market model over event days -5 to +5

key_ivs.name: method of payment interacted with type of acquisition (merger vs tender offer)
key_ivs.measure: method of payment (stock exchange, cash, or combination) cross-classified with 126 merger proposals vs 41 tender offers
key_ivs.source: Wall Street Journal Index and SEC forms 13D and 14D

analyses.label: Table V - Abnormal Returns for Unsuccessful Bids (12 unsuccessful stock exchange offers vs 47 unsuccessful cash offers)

dv.name: bidding firms' common stock abnormal returns
dv.measure: daily average abnormal return (AR) and cumulative abnormal return (CAR) around the initial announcement, event days -5 to +5

key_ivs.name: method of payment (stock exchange offer vs cash offer)
key_ivs.source: Wall Street Journal Index and W. T. Grimm & Co. Mergerstat Review

analyses.label: Table VI - Abnormal Returns of Bidding Firms' Nonconvertible Bonds (12 stock exchange offers = 24 bonds vs 16 cash offers = 28 bonds); wealth-transfer test
analyses.sample: thirty bidding firms with fifty-eight publicly traded nonconvertible bond issues: twelve stock exchange offers (24 bonds) and sixteen cash offers (28 bonds), 1972-1981

dv.name: nonconvertible bond abnormal returns of bidding firms
dv.measure: daily average abnormal return (AR) of nonconvertible bonds; daily bond returns computed from closing prices including daily accrued interest, event days -5 to +5

key_ivs.name: method of payment (stock exchange offer vs cash offer)
key_ivs.source: Wall Street Journal Index and SEC forms 13D and 14D
